Expressions of Interest - Lecturers - School of Media, Film and Journalism - Multiple Opportunities

Location: Caulfield campus

Employment Type: Continuing

Remuneration: $123,138 - $146,228 pa Level B (plus 17% employer superannuation) and $150,841 - $173,931 pa Level C (plus 17% employer superannuation)

  • Amplify your impact at a world top 50 University
  • Join our inclusive, collaborative community
  • Be surrounded by extraordinary ideas - and the people who discover them

In the Faculty of Arts at Monash University (Melbourne, Australia), we believe great teaching and innovative research can change lives and shape resilient societies. Our vibrant and internationally recognised Faculty offers an excellent opportunity to work in an ambitious, collaborative and diverse scholarly environment that values excellence, innovation and impact. Most importantly, it is a place where scholars are empowered to pursue ambitious, purpose-driven research and education that makes a meaningful difference to communities locally and globally. Come and accelerate your career with us. Develop your academic career in the School of Media, Film and Journalism where your scholarship and teaching can make a global difference

The Opportunity

We’re seeking multiple ambitious early and mid-career academics to join our growing School of Media, Film and Journalism, based in the Faculty of Arts in Melbourne, Australia. In MFJ, you will join an inclusive and collaborative research community focused on media, film, communications, journalism and storytelling, where creativity leads, ideas connect, and research and teaching shapes global communication and impact.

You’ll have the opportunity to work alongside internationally recognised scholars, including in the world-leading research centres of the Monash Climate Communication Hub and the Constructive Institute Asia Pacific. You will be supported through mentorship, collaboration and career development opportunities to shape inspiring student experiences, build a dynamic research profile and contribute to work that creates meaningful impact beyond the university.

Where ever you are in the world, if you’re excited by an opportunity to contribute to a leading global university and help shape the future of Monash Arts, then we’d love to hear from you!

About the Positions

As a Level B Lecturer or Level C Senior Lecturer in the Faculty of Arts, you’ll inspire the next generation through creative educational offerings, while building your research profile, and pursuing external funding opportunities. We are particularly interested in the following
disciplinary/interdisciplinary areas:

  • Film, Screen and Culture
  • Media
  • Communications

Your key responsibilities will include:

  • Impactful Research: Maintain and expand a strong track record of refereed publications and competitive grant capture, to develop cutting-edge research in your field.
  • Innovative Teaching and Coordination: Design, coordinate, and deliver engaging undergraduate and postgraduate units.
  • Student Mentorship: Lead lectures, tutorials, and field excursions, while supervising Honours and postgraduate coursework and research students.
  • Community and Collaboration: Actively contribute to the academic life of the section and school through collaborative initiatives, service duties, and engagement with external organisations.

What you will bring:

  • Qualifications: A PhD degree in a relevant discipline
  • Research Capability: Proven commitment to scholarly research, including strong manuscript preparation, high-quality publications, and willingness to pursue external research funding.
  • Teaching Excellence: A demonstrated track record of tertiary teaching, curriculum development, and an ability to motivate and actively engage students.
  • Collegiate Spirit: Excellent interpersonal skills with a proven ability to work cooperatively across teams, students, and external partners.

To Apply

Diversity is one of our greatest strengths at Monash Arts. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people, culturally and linguistically diverse people, people with disabilities, neurodivergent people, and people of all genders, sexualities, and age groups.

Apply now via the following appropriate link:

title: Expression of Interest - Sessional Academics in Banking and Finance
description: Join our dynamic academic team as a sessional academic and contribute your industry expertise to the education of tomorrow’s finance leaders.

Expression of Interest - Sessional Academics in Banking and Finance

Job No.: 701042

Location: Caulfield and/or Clayton campus

Employment Type: Sessional

Remuneration: Sessional rates will apply

  • Be inspired, every day
  • Take your career in exciting, rewarding directions
  • Be a part of an inclusive, collaborative community

The Opportunity

Are you a finance professional with a passion for teaching? The Department of Banking and Finance in the Faculty of Business and Economics invites applications for sessional academics to join our dynamic academic team. This is an exciting opportunity to contribute
your industry expertise to the education of tomorrow’s finance leaders.

Key Responsibilities

  • Deliver engaging teaching activities in Banking and Finance courses
  • Develop and update learning materials and incorporate real-world case studies
  • Mark and assess student assignments, exams and other coursework in line with established rubrics
  • Provide timely, constructive feedback to support student learning and professional growth
  • Maintain academic integrity and uphold the high teaching standards of the Monash Business School

About You

We are seeking candidates who possess strong academic qualifications in Finance, holding a Master degree or higher, combined with recent or current experience in the banking, finance, or broader commercial sector. The ideal applicant will demonstrate the ability to
integrate practical industry insights into their teaching practice, enriching the learning experience for our students. Effective communication skills and a genuine enthusiasm for engaging with a diverse student cohort are essential, along with a commitment to delivering high-quality, student-centred education. The successful candidate will be self-motivated, detail-oriented, and capable of working both independently and as part of a collaborative academic team. Familiarity with digital learning platforms and contemporary teaching tools will be considered an advantage.

About the Monash Business School

Monash Business School is consistently ranked in the world’s top 100 for Business and Management and is renowned for its research excellence and global outlook. Our Department of Banking and Finance offers a vibrant, supportive environment where
academic rigor meets practical relevance. 

To Apply:

Please submit a current copy of your resume along with a cover letter in which you address how you meet the requirements of the role as outlined in the advertisement.

Enquiries: Dr Zhe An, Senior Lecturer in Banking and Finance, zhe.an@monash.edu

Applications Close: Monday 30th November 2026, 11:55 pm AEDT

title: Specialist - Psychosocial Risk
description: Monash University is seeking a Specialist - Psychosocial Risk to play a pivotal role in driving a safe, supportive and thriving workplace culture

Specialist - Psychosocial Risk

Job No.: 699031

Location: Clayton campus

Employment Type: Full-time

Duration: Continuing appointment

Remuneration: $124,343 - $137,251 pa HEW Level 08 (plus 17% employer superannuation)

  • Amplify your impact at a world top 50 University
  • Join our inclusive, collaborative community
  • Be surrounded by extraordinary ideas - and the people who discover them

The Opportunity

Monash University is seeking a Specialist - Psychosocial Risk to play a pivotal role in driving a safe, supportive and thriving workplace culture. Reporting to the Manager - Psychosocial Risk and collaborating with Health, Safety & Wellbeing, HR and the Safer Community Unit, you will lead the implementation of proactive systems, training and programs that mitigate psychosocial hazards and ensure full compliance with OHS legislation and Victorian Psychological Health Regulations.

As a trusted adviser across all levels of the University, you will provide practical, authoritative advice on risk management and deliver capability-building resources. Your responsibilities include managing hazard reporting systems, conducting risk assessments and investigations and monitoring key performance indicators to generate data insights for executive reporting and continuous wellbeing improvements.

To excel, you will hold relevant postgraduate qualifications or equivalent senior expertise, backed by extensive experience in psychosocial risk management and occupational health legislation. You bring a strong background in managing complex projects, conducting risk assessments and leveraging data within large organisations. Exceptional communication, analytical and stakeholder management skills will enable you to influence outcomes and translate complex concepts into practical, high-impact solutions.

About Monash University

At Monash, work feels different. There’s a sense of belonging, from contributing to something ground breaking – a place where great things happen.

We value difference and diversity. That’s why we champion an inclusive and respectful workplace culture where everyone is supported to succeed.

Some 20,000 staff work for Monash around the world. We have 95,000 students, four Australian campuses, and campuses in Malaysia and Indonesia. We also have a major presence in India and China, and a significant centre and research foundation in Italy.

In our short history, we have skyrocketed through global university rankings and established ourselves consistently among the world's best tertiary institutions. We rank in the world’s top-50 universities in rankings including the QS World University Rankings 2026.

Learn more about Monash.

Today, we have the momentum to create the future we need for generations to come. Accelerate your change here. 

Monash supports flexible and hybrid working arrangements. We have a range of policies in place enabling staff to combine work and personal commitments. This includes supporting parents.
